Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 19-year-old female with 3 days of stinging dysuria, mild lower abdominal cramping specifically with urination, mild hematuria this morning, and abnormal urine odor.
- No increased urinary frequency/urgency, no fever, no back/flank pain, no nausea/vomiting, no abnormal vaginal discharge, bowel habits normal.
- Past history of IBS; no significant family history.
- Sexually active (condom use); new boyfriend of two months; no prior STD screen.
- Assessment consistent with uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
- Offered empiric antibiotic treatment (Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim; dose/route/frequency not documented) for 3 days.
- Provided safety netting advice: seek further review if symptoms persist, worsen, or if fever/back pain develops due to risk of ascending infection.
- Suggested avoiding sexual activity until symptoms resolve; advised to continue barrier contraception.
- Advised to maintain good hydration and consider cranberry juice.
- Pregnancy unlikely, but advised to test if uncertainty arises.

Management Plan
- Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim for 3 days (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Increase fluid intake.
- Avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve.
- Continue using condoms.
- Advise use of cranberry juice.
- Advised to return/call if symptoms persist, worsen, or new symptoms (fever, back/flank pain) develop.
- Consider pregnancy testing if suspicion arises.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis): High likelihood. Classic symptoms—dysuria, mild hematuria, lower abdominal pain, abnormal urine odor—in sexually active young woman. Transcript and DDx fully consistent.
- Sexually transmitted infection/urethritis (e.g., chlamydia, gonorrhea): Moderate likelihood. Supported by new sexual partner and no prior STD screening, but less likely due to lack of discharge and use of condoms. Consistent with both transcript and DDx.
- Renal/urinary tract stone: Low likelihood. Hematuria and dysuria noted, but absence of severe/radiating pain and no back/flank pain. Aligned with transcript and DDx.
